f74r.summary: Written after Moray's murder at Linlithgow (23 Jan 1570): Mary tells Norfolk she will undertake nothing unless it is safe for them both, urges him to write and to act through his sister Scrope or others, says Elizabeth gives her the blame ('veyt') for Moray's death, reports rumours of Morton and Lord Talbot, and begs him not to risk writing in his own hand.

snip.cap: BL Cotton MS Caligula C II f. 74r, the left half of the first five cipher lines of Mary to Norfolk, the 20th [1570]: I have, my oun good lord
